# What the AICR lanes refuse

**UNOFFICIAL/EXPERIMENTAL.** Generated by
`npm run aicr-refusal-corpus:generate` and checked by
`npm run aicr-refusal-corpus:verify`. The corpus this reads is hand-authored
at `examples/aicr/refusal-corpus/candidates.yaml`, and the run that
produced these verdicts is recorded at `runs/aicr-refusal-corpus/receipt.yaml`.

Each candidate below is a change someone could reasonably propose to an AICR
entry. Every one was applied to a throwaway worktree of the commit under test
and run through the shipped commands, unmodified. Two candidates had to be accepted,
because lanes that refused everything would look identical to lanes that
refused the right things.

| Candidate | Declared | Verdict | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unmodified-tree` | accepted | accepted | nothing, as declared |
| `entry-prose-edited` | accepted | accepted | nothing, as declared |
| `retained-application-edited` | refused | refused | `digest-index` |
| `retained-edit-then-regenerated` | refused | refused | `digest-index`, `digest-index:generate` |
| `credential-retained-with-consistent-checksum` | refused | refused | `kserve-nim-index` |
| `control-point-token-copied-into-a-second-document` | refused | refused | `digest-index`, `blast-radius` |
| `control-point-token-removed-from-a-governed-document` | refused | refused | `digest-index`, `blast-radius` |
| `sync-wave-reordered` | refused | refused | `digest-index`, `ordering-parity` |
| `attested-subject-bytes-edited` | refused | refused | `signature-subject` |

## Which lane said what

A refusal is more informative when you can also see what stayed quiet. This
matrix is the same run, per lane.

| Candidate | digest-index | inference-nim-index | kserve-nim-index | blast-radius | ordering-parity | signature-subject |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unmodified-tree` | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `entry-prose-edited` | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `retained-application-edited` | refused | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `retained-edit-then-regenerated` | refused | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `credential-retained-with-consistent-checksum` | accepted | accepted | refused | accepted | accepted | accepted |
| `control-point-token-copied-into-a-second-document` | refused | accepted | accepted | refused | accepted | accepted |
| `control-point-token-removed-from-a-governed-document` | refused | accepted | accepted | refused | accepted | accepted |
| `sync-wave-reordered` | refused | accepted | accepted | accepted | refused | accepted |
| `attested-subject-bytes-edited` | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | accepted | refused |

The pattern in that matrix is worth reading rather than skimming.
`digest-index` guards the widest surface, and it caught 5 of the
7 refused candidates on its own. The 2 it did not catch are
`credential-retained-with-consistent-checksum` and `attested-subject-bytes-edited`. Both of those
are internally consistent changes rather than drift, which is exactly the case
a checksum cannot see and a rule has to.

## The rules and what exercises them

Every rule declared in the corpus has a candidate behind it. The loader refuses
a corpus where a rule has none, so this table cannot silently go empty.

| Rule | Lane | Exercised by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retained-bytes-parity` | `digest-index` | `retained-application-edited` |
| `retention-is-not-regenerable` | `digest-index:generate` | `retained-edit-then-regenerated` |
| `credential-boundary` | `kserve-nim-index` | `credential-retained-with-consistent-checksum` |
| `control-point-undeclared-reach` | `blast-radius` | `control-point-token-copied-into-a-second-document` |
| `control-point-stale-declaration` | `blast-radius` | `control-point-token-removed-from-a-governed-document` |
| `upstream-ordering-parity` | `ordering-parity` | `sync-wave-reordered` |
| `attested-subject-binding` | `signature-subject` | `attested-subject-bytes-edited` |

## What each refusal actually said

- `retained-application-edited`, refused by `digest-index`:
  > argocd-rendered/templates/cert-manager.yaml differs from argocd-rendered/checksums.txt; the rendered surface drifted
- `retained-edit-then-regenerated`, refused by `digest-index:generate`:
  > argocd-rendered/templates/cert-manager.yaml differs from argocd-rendered/checksums.txt; the rendered surface drifted
- `credential-retained-with-consistent-checksum`, refused by `kserve-nim-index`:
  > upstream/kserve/nim-models/llama-3.1-8b-instruct_1xgpu_1.1.0.yaml: a literal credential value is assigned to NGC_API_KEY; secret surfaces must carry names or substitutions only
- `control-point-token-copied-into-a-second-document`, refused by `blast-radius`:
  > examples/aicr/control-points/eks-h100-training-kubeflow.yaml: control point prometheus-storage-class also reaches argoproj.io/v1alpha1|Application|argocd|gpu-operator, which the record does not declare
- `control-point-token-removed-from-a-governed-document`, refused by `blast-radius`:
  > examples/aicr/control-points/eks-h100-training-kubeflow.yaml: control point prometheus-storage-class declares argoproj.io/v1alpha1|Application|argocd|kube-prometheus-stack, which does not contain its locator
- `sync-wave-reordered`, refused by `ordering-parity`:
  > examples/aicr/eks-h100-training-kubeflow: gpu-operator is in wave 8 and depends on cert-manager in wave 97, so the rendered waves would run it too early
- `attested-subject-bytes-edited`, refused by `signature-subject`:
  > examples/aicr/upstream-signatures/v0.18.0/attested-subject/registry.yaml differs from its recorded checksum

## What this proves and what it does not

It proves the shipped commands refuse these shapes today, and that they accept
changes outside the surfaces they claim to guard. It does not prove the corpus
is complete. A shape nobody thought to propose is not covered, and the honest
reading of a green run here is that the listed rules hold, not that the entries
are unbreakable.

Everything ran offline against committed configuration bytes. No cluster, no
organization, and no network took part, and no credential named in the corpus
is real.
